selected_evidence.requirement: New interactive login sessions use umask 027
selected_evidence.summary: Configuration was installed, and root plus non-root interactive login tests reported umask 0027 with runtime permission assertions passing.

Healthy baseline boot ID 8e0ddb92-5f82-4d03-942e-362c27d766cd was captured, reboot acknowledged, and node1 returned with boot ID ab6db6f2-1ad2-4ef7-873e-e96f9d2fc08e. Required targets, writable storage, configuration, and runtime umask behavior all recovered.

--- pam_umask manual excerpt ---
PAM_UMASK(8)			Linux-PAM Manual		   PAM_UMASK(8)

NAME
       pam_umask - PAM module to set the file mode creation mask

SYNOPSIS

       pam_umask.so [debug] [silent] [usergroups] [nousergroups] [umask=mask]

DESCRIPTION
       pam_umask is a PAM module to set the file mode creation mask of the
       current environment. The umask affects the default permissions assigned
       to newly created files.

       The PAM module tries to get the umask value from the following places in
       the following order:

       •   umask= entry in the user's GECOS field (see below for details)

       •   umask= argument

       •   UMASK entry from /etc/login.defs

       •   UMASK= entry from /etc/default/login

       The GECOS field is split on comma ',' characters. Entries must be set in
       its 'other' (sub-)field (the 5th field within the GECOS field), which
       could be done, for example, using chfn --other. In addition to the
       umask= entry, the module also recognizes the pri= entry, which sets the
       nice priority value for the session, and the ulimit= entry, which sets
       the maximum size of files the processes in the session can create.

OPTIONS
       debug
	   Print debug information.

       silent
	   Don't print informative messages.

       usergroups
	   If the user is not root and the username is the same as primary
	   group name, the umask group bits are set to be the same as owner
	   bits (examples: 022 -> 002, 077 -> 007).

       nousergroups
	   This is the direct opposite of the usergroups option described
	   above, which can be useful in case pam_umask has been compiled with
	   usergroups enabled by default and you want to disable it at runtime.

       umask=mask
	   Sets the calling process's file mode creation mask (umask) to mask &
	   0777. The value is interpreted as Octal.

MODULE TYPES PROVIDED
       Only the session type is provided.

RETURN VALUES
       PAM_SUCCESS
	   The new umask was set successfully.

       PAM_BUF_ERR
	   M

commands.command:
set -eu
[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]
for f in /etc/login.defs /etc/pam.d/common-session; do
  if [ ! -e "$f.antrieb-umask027.bak" ]; then cp -a "$f" "$f.antrieb-umask027.bak"; fi
done
if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*UMASK[[:space:]]+' /etc/login.defs; then
  sed -i -E 's/^[[:space:]]*UMASK[[:space:]]+.*/UMASK\t\t027/' /etc/login.defs
else
  printf '\n# Secure default for new login sessions.\nUMASK\t\t027\n' >> /etc/login.defs
fi
sed -i -E 's|^[[:space:]]*session[[:space:]]+optional[[:space:]]+pam_umask\.so([[:space:]].*)?$|session optional\t\t\tpam_umask.so umask=027 nousergroups|' /etc/pam.d/common-session
umask_file_tmp=$(mktemp /etc/profile.d/.secure-umask.XXXXXX)
printf '%s\n' '# Secure default for interactive login shells; user startup files may override it.' 'umask 027' > "$umask_file_tmp"
chmod 0644 "$umask_file_tmp"
chown root:root "$umask_file_tmp"
mv "$umask_file_tmp" /etc/profile.d/secure-umask.sh
printf '%s\n' 'configuration_written'
grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*UMASK[[:space:]]+' /etc/login.defs
grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*session[[:space:]]+optional[[:space:]]+pam_umask\.so' /etc/pam.d/common-session
stat -c '%n owner=%U:%G mode=%a' /etc/profile.d/secure-umask.sh
sed -n '1,5p' /etc/profile.d/secure-umask.sh

commands.command:
set -eu
verify_script=$(mktemp /tmp/verify-umask-login.XXXXXX)
cat > "$verify_script" <<'ANTRIEB_VERIFY'
case $- in
  *i*) printf 'interactive_shell=yes\n' ;;
  *) printf 'interactive_shell=no\n'; exit 1 ;;
esac
if shopt -q login_shell; then printf 'login_shell=yes\n'; else printf 'login_shell=no\n'; exit 1; fi
printf 'effective_umask=%s\n' "$(umask)"
test_dir=/tmp/umask027-runtime-test-$$
mkdir "$test_dir"
: > "$test_dir/file"
dir_mode=$(stat -c %a "$test_dir")
file_mode=$(stat -c %a "$test_dir/file")
printf 'created_directory_mode=%s\ncreated_file_mode=%s\n' "$dir_mode" "$file_mode"
[ "$(umask)" = 0027 ]
[ "$dir_mode" = 750 ]
[ "$file_mode" = 640 ]
unlink "$test_dir/file"
rmdir "$test_dir"
printf 'runtime_assertions=passed\n'
ANTRIEB_VERIFY
chmod 0755 "$verify_script"
TERM=dumb su -l root -s /bin/bash -c "bash --login --interactive -c '. $verify_script'"
unlink "$verify_script"

set -eu
verify_script=$(mktemp /tmp/verify-umask-nonroot.XXXXXX)
trap 'unlink "$verify_script" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
cat > "$verify_script" <<'ANTRIEB_VERIFY'
printf 'session_user=%s primary_group=%s\n' "$(id -un)" "$(id -gn)"
case $- in
  *i*) printf 'interactive_shell=yes\n' ;;
  *) printf 'interactive_shell=no\n'; exit 1 ;;
esac
if shopt -q login_shell; then printf 'login_shell=yes\n'; else printf 'login_shell=no\n'; exit 1; fi
mask=$(umask)
printf 'effective_umask=%s\n' "$mask"
test_dir=/tmp/umask027-nonroot-$$
cleanup_test_dir() {
  if [ -e "$test_dir/file" ]; then unlink "$test_dir/file"; fi
  if [ -d "$test_dir" ]; then rmdir "$test_dir"; fi
}
trap cleanup_test_dir EXIT
mkdir "$test_dir"
: > "$test_dir/file"
dir_mode=$(stat -c %a "$test_dir")
file_mode=$(stat -c %a "$test_dir/file")
printf 'created_directory_mode=%s\ncreated_file_mode=%s\n' "$dir_mode" "$file_mode"
[ "$(id -un)" = daemon ]
[ "$(id -gn)" = daemon ]
[ "$mask" = 0027 ]
[ "$dir_mode" = 750 ]
[ "$file_mode" = 640 ]
printf 'nonroot_runtime_assertions=passed\n'
ANTRIEB_VERIFY
chmod 0755 "$verify_script"
TERM=dumb su -s /bin/bash daemon -c "bash -lic '. $verify_script'"
commands.stdout:

bash: no job control in this shell
session_user=daemon primary_group=daemon
interactive_shell=yes
login_shell=yes
effective_umask=0027
created_directory_mode=750
created_file_mode=640
nonroot_runtime_assertions=passed
